summary: Life on the island is now the strongest part of the game. Three sessions brought whole-island events: Big Boing, FREEZE!, conga, roll call, and now the Big Sneeze, which you can trigger yourself with X: 140 gold feathers burst out, friends tumble, and the feathers stay on the grass. The traced sneeze still (site/img/big-sneeze.png) is the funniest picture the game has made. What you see during play has not changed since s61: the eye-level and overview progress shots are identical (same flat noon green, same primitive friends). Name tags still float over tree crowns, hide and seek still leaves a found friend 13.7 m behind, and the follow camera still shoots straight down.

lighting.why: The raster noon is still evenly lit saturated green with grey-blue shadows and no haze; eye-level s64 is pixel-for-pixel the s61 composition. Only the traced frames look warm.

world.why: Overview and eye-level identical to s61: no new place, terrain or water change in three sessions. The yellow flower field reads as flat paint from above.

props.why: 36 generated assets and the cottage, trees and rocks hold up. The new things are built from primitives: the sneeze feathers are flat yellow ovals like paper confetti, and the Big Boing toadstool is a red sphere cap with white dots (orbit.png corner).

creatures.why: Lumi is a real character in traced frames. The friends are still a sphere and tube legs (the pig in big-sneeze.png), green/cyan balls with googly eyes, and a cotton sheep; their behaviour (gasp, fly, hunt feathers, wear them) is now better than their bodies.

fun.why: + The sneeze is a player-triggered event that involves the whole island. - Still the same three mini games; hide and seek's first play fails exactly as at s61 (friend 13.7 m behind); firefly first play failed once right after a sneeze.

wow.why: +1: the Big Sneeze is the first stunt a stranger would share (feather burst, friends blown head over heels). Live it is watched from ~15 m away, so the flights are tiny; the traced still sells it far better than the game does.

camera.why: The traced view at 11:40 looked straight down at the dance ring, with a creature's flower hat filling the middle (traced.png); the sneeze is framed wide and from above; the cuts themselves are fine.

ui.why: 'Truffle' floats over a tree crown with no Truffle in view (orbit.png); Lumi's thought bubble hangs over a tree or the cottage while Lumi is off screen (follow2.png, orbit.png); during the sneeze three speech lines stack into one unreadable block (sneeze4.png).

style.why: Clay-toy trees, cottage and rocks are cohesive; the flat-shaded feathers, the sphere toadstool and the primitive friends break it.

performance.why: Sandbox frame median 3.6 ms, p95 7.4 ms with 50+ systems; the sneeze costs 0.3 ms.

findings.title: Friends as lovable as Lumi: a silhouette and face per species
findings.what: In the best picture the game has (the traced sneeze) Lumi is a feathered bird, and next to it Sir Sniffsalot is a pink sphere with four sausage legs, Gloop a green ball with googly eyes, the crab a cone on sticks. The friends now act out the best moments (blown away, feather hunts) but look like placeholders doing it.
findings.suggestion: One species per session, like Lumi got: a generated or sculpted body with a recognisable silhouette (snout and ears for the Snootle, a real shell and claws for the Crabbit, a fleece with a face for the Fluffkin), proper faces.jl expressions, and one signature move each.
findings.done_when: A tools/lineup.jl traced lineup shows every species with its own non-sphere silhouette; a stranger can name each animal from a 64 px thumbnail.

findings.title: Raster lighting: warm sun, soft coloured shadows, haze, readable noon
findings.what: What players actually see (the raster) is flat noon green with grey shadows, while the traced frames of the same island are warm and soft. media/progress session-0061 and session-0064 eye-level show the same lighting.
findings.suggestion: Fix it where the limit is: a warm key colour, sky-tinted (blue) shadow fill and distance fog in the RayMakie raster shader, so the raster comes close to the traced look.
findings.done_when: eye-level.png at 11:30: mean shadow hue clearly blue-shifted vs lit grass, far trees lighter/desaturated than near ones, and a side-by-side with a traced still of the same camera looks like the same game.

findings.title: A new place north of the pond that the overview shows
findings.what: Three sessions of whole-island events, but the island itself has not grown: the overview and eye-level progress shots are the same as s61. A player who comes back sees the same meadow, pond, cottage and beach.
findings.where: north of the pond (in front of the overview camera); meadow.jl regions
findings.suggestion: A place with its own look and a reason to go there: a little waterfall and stream from a rocky rise, a hilltop lookout with a ruin, or a mossy glade with glowing mushrooms at night. Use generated assets and its own terrain colour, and give it a pastime the creatures use there.
findings.done_when: The overview progress shot shows a new, clearly different area; at least one creature pastime happens there (an event kind in the log).

findings.title: Real feathers and a real Big Boing toadstool
findings.what: The sneeze's 140 feathers are flat, evenly yellow ellipse discs; while they fly they read as confetti or leaves, and on the grass as yellow paint dabs. The Big Boing toadstool is a sphere cap with dots whose spots vanish in path tracing.
findings.suggestion: A small feather mesh (quill + curved vane, light, instanced) that flutters down (sway + spin) instead of falling like a plate; a generated toadstool asset with a carved cap and spots.
findings.done_when: A close screenshot of feathers on the grass shows quills and a curved vane; the toadstool in a traced still shows its spots.

findings.title: Follow camera: no fence or crown across the frame, no shots straight down
findings.what: At 11:40 the follow camera looked straight down at the dance ring: friends seen as tops of heads, a flower hat filling the middle of the frame. A live sneeze is framed from ~15 m and high, so the friends' head-over-heels flights are a few pixels.
findings.where: render.jl camera_goal / dancecircle CAMERA_GROUPS, sneeze.jl sneeze_group
findings.suggestion: Clamp the pitch of every auto view (no more than ~35° down), and for the sneeze cut to a low, close side view that keeps Lumi and the nearest two flyers in frame, the way the traced still does.
findings.done_when: A 3-minute sampled run of the follow camera (a screenshot every 10 s) has no view steeper than 35°, and a live sneeze screenshot shows at least two airborne friends larger than 60 px.

findings.title: Hide and seek: found friends keep up with the seeker
findings.what: The first-play test fails today with exactly the s61 numbers: 'found friends lag: 13.7, 2.8 m'. The game's promise, a growing parade of found friends, breaks with the first friend.
findings.evidence: live_tests('a first play') at 11:42: Hide and seek failed 'found friends lag: Float32[13.7, 2.8] m'
findings.suggestion: Found friends run (fast) to their slot when more than 3 m away, and say something funny when they catch up.
findings.done_when: The hide and seek first-play test passes 3 runs in a row with both lags < 4 m.

findings.title: Name tags and thought bubble sit on their own creature
findings.what: 'Truffle' floats over a tree crown with no Truffle in view; Lumi's 'A feather tickles my beak' bubble hangs over a tree / the cottage while Lumi is hidden or off screen; during the sneeze 'Truffle', 'My ears', 'Lumi' and a speech line stack into one block.
findings.suggestion: Hide the tag/bubble when its creature is occluded or off screen (or pin it to the screen edge with an arrow), and push overlapping labels apart vertically.
findings.done_when: In 10 orbit/follow screenshots no tag or bubble is drawn without its creature visible under it, and no two labels overlap.

findings.title: A sneeze's end must not hand the steered Lumi a new goal
findings.what: Firefly catch's first play, started right after a sneeze (sneeze state :after), caught 0 flies: Lumi moved 1.2 m in 20 s with W held. Run again later (sneeze :idle) it passed in 15 s. sneeze.jl finish! calls NG.choose_goal! on Lumi even when it is controlled, which happens exactly when a mini game starts.
findings.evidence: live_tests('a first play') 11:42: 'W/A/D play caught 0 flies ... Lumi at (-1.46, 5.77) start (-1.29, 4.63)'; passed alone at 11:45
findings.suggestion: Skip controlled creatures in finish!, and leave_interactions!/face_open! Lumi when a mini game takes it mid-sneeze.
findings.done_when: A test that starts the firefly first play during a sneeze's :after phase catches 3 flies in 20 s.

todos.why: Sessions 62-64 added five shared island moments (boing, freeze, conga, roll call, the sneeze with feather hunts); seen live.
site/img/workshop-traced.png exists and is in the workshop post in site/index.html.
Still true: jumped in as Lumi, the player can sneeze but cannot fetch and give a present.
Lumi's walk and celebrations are still the generic poses; #394 is one piece of it.
Deliveries are still a crate on Lumi's head.
Not re-tested at night this review; the emissive leak patch is still open.

engine.what: The RayMakie raster has no coloured sky fill or distance fog, and it ignores AmbientLight, so the raster cannot come close to the traced look from plugins alone (todo #237).
engine.evidence: CLAUDE.md lesson s45; media/progress/session-0064/eye-level.png vs site/img/big-sneeze.png

engine.what: live_path_tracing(true) + one screenshot + false took 3m54s (40 s of it a sleep): turning the trace on and off in the sandbox stalls the live commands for minutes.

process: Sessions 62-64 put real work into goal 1 (whole-island events, the player-triggered sneeze) and goal 5 (Lumi's pages, voice, self). Goal 2 has a release (a 40 s voiced day film, soft at 960x540/40 spp but a real film). The work is fun to read about, but it piles up as event systems on an island that looks the same: lighting, the friends' bodies and the camera (#236, #237, #239, all high or medium since s52-s61) got no work, and the eye-level shot is unchanged. Each event is also less visible than its journal entry, because the live camera watches it from afar. Next sessions: one species body (#236), one raster lighting pass in RayMakie (#237) and one new area before a sixth island party. Goal 3 (physics, spray paint, Maelstrom water) has had no work at all and needs a first step.
